R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-62) and Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds, ch. 111-8-63), permitted by DCH Healthcare Facility Regulation Division; Medicaid via the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP / SOURCE Alternative Living Services)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates as a licensed Georgia **Personal Care Home (PCH, 2–24 beds, Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 111-8-62)** or **Assisted Living Community (ALC, 25+ beds, ch. 111-8-63)**. Delete whichever does not apply, and complete the Medicaid sections only if **[AGENCY NAME]** participates in the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP / SOURCE Alternative Living Services).

The manual is meant to:

- Turn the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH) rules into written, day-to-day procedures that staff can follow.
- Support resident dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy, which the governing body must promote through its policies (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07).
- Give the governing body, administrator or on-site manager, and staff one shared reference for admissions, resident care, medications, emergencies, reporting and records.
- Give DCH inspectors a current set of policies. The DCH ALC Application Checklist notes that communities are inspected without notice and that policies must be available for review.

**Important:** This manual is a template. It does not replace the rules themselves, and it is not legal advice. Several rules cited here were only partly retrieved when this manual was prepared. Before adoption, read the full current text of every rule on which a policy depends.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

1. **Customize.** Replace every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder and every bracketed item (for example license class, capacity, floors occupied, memory care status, Medicaid participation, named staff positions, phone numbers). Make the manual match your actual permit, your licensed residential care profile and the services you really provide.
2. **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the adoption date and any later approvals in the minutes. The governing body is responsible for oversight of compliance (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07; 111-8-62-.07).
3. **Keep current.** Review the manual at least annually, and sooner when a rule is amended, DCH issues new guidance, your license class or services change, or an inspection or incident shows a gap. Rule .09 of Ch. 111-8-63 was amended effective May 21, 2025, so check every staffing and training policy against current text. Keep prior versions with their effective dates.
4. **Train staff.** Every staff member must be trained on the policies that apply to their role and must sign an acknowledgment. Keep the training records. Orientation and ongoing training are governing-body policy topics under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07 and 111-8-62-.07, and training records are required under 111-8-63-.09.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**Who should use it.** Owners and governing body members, the administrator or on-site manager, direct care staff, certified medication aides, nursing staff (RN/LPN), and anyone who supervises or trains staff.

**Structure.** Policies follow the order of the rules so that each one can be traced to its source. Each policy should state its purpose, who is responsible, the procedure, the records to keep, and the rule it implements. Suggested sections:

| Topic | Primary rule(s) |
|---|---|
| Permit, ownership and licensure | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.05, 111-8-63-.06, 111-8-62-.05, 111-8-62-.06 |
| Governing body and policies | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07, 111-8-62-.07 |
| Workforce, training and staffing | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09, 111-8-62-.08, 111-8-62-.09 |
| Accountability and inspections | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.10 |
| Furnishings and safety | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.12, 111-8-63-.13 |
| Emergency preparedness | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.14 |
| Admission, agreements and services | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.15, 111-8-63-.16, 111-8-63-.17 |
| Memory care (if certified) | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.19; O.C.G.A. § 31-7-12.4 |
| Medications | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.20 |
| Nutrition | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.21 |
| Resident files and rights | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.24, 111-8-63-.25 |
| Change in condition | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.26 |
| Discharge and transfer | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.29 |
| Reports to DCH | Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.30 |

**Steps for implementation.**

1. Confirm your license class (PCH or ALC), capacity, floors in use and whether you hold or advertise a memory care certificate. Remove policies that do not apply.
2. Where the ALC rule (ch. 111-8-63) is cited and you operate a PCH, compare it with the matching PCH rule in ch. 111-8-62. The PCH rules are described as mirroring the ALC rules, but only rules .01–.06 of ch. 111-8-62 were read in full when this manual was prepared. Verify the PCH text for every policy.
3. Fill in all [AGENCY NAME] placeholders, names of responsible positions, phone numbers and posting locations.
4. Resolve the items flagged **"verify"** in the Regulatory Framework section before the governing body adopts the manual.
5. Have the governing body adopt the manual, then train all staff and file signed acknowledgments.
6. Keep a current copy where staff can reach it and available for DCH review. Keep the posted items the rules require (permit, latest inspection report and plan of correction, evacuation maps, ombudsman contact, disaster plan access).
7. Review the manual on a set schedule and whenever the rules change. Record each revision.

**Conventions.** "Administrator or on-site manager" means the person responsible for daily operations under the rules. "Representative or legal surrogate" has the meaning in the definitions rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.03 and 111-8-62-.03). Use the defined terms exactly as the rules do.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Legal authority

- **O.C.G.A. §§ 31-2-7 and Chapter 7 of Title 31**: statutory authority for the ALC rules (Rule 111-8-63-.01). The Rule .09 notes also cite O.C.G.A. 31-2-8, 31-2-9, 31-7-1 et seq. and 43-26-12.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62** (PCH): legal authority is O.C.G.A. Title 31, Chapters 2 and 7. A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license.

### Governing rules

The cite text below is quoted exactly as given in the source list. Descriptions are summaries only. Read the full current rule before relying on it.

**Assisted Living Communities (25+ beds)**

- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63**: Rules and Regulations for Assisted Living Communities (rules .01–.34).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.03**: Definitions (for example abuse, injury, assistive device, restraints, limited nursing services, memory care center, medical alert system, proxy caregiver, owner at 10% or more interest).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.05**: Application for Permit (DCH forms and fees, floor plan, ownership disclosure, zoning, CPA financial stability affidavit for initial applications).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.06**: Permits (valid permit before admitting residents, display, non-transferable, capacity limit, marketing of licensure classification).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.07**: Owner Governance (governing body oversight and minimum policy topics). *Verify:* the list of required policies was truncated in the retrieved text. Read the full paragraph before finalizing.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.09**: Workforce Qualifications, Training and Staffing (amended eff. May 21, 2025): age rules, training within 60 days, first aid/CPR, continuing education hours, background checks, personnel files, staffing ratios, RN/LPN on-site hours, staffing records, ID badges, medical alert system.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.10**: Community Accountability (inspector access to records, 10-day dispute and plan-of-correction deadlines, posting of the latest inspection report, licensed residential care profile, memory care certificate).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.12**: Community Furnishings. *Verify:* only some paragraphs were visible.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.13**: Community Safety Precautions. *Verify:* only paragraphs (1), (11) and (12) were visible. Fire drill and other paragraphs were not retrieved.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.14**: Emergency Preparedness (compliance with Ch. 111-8-16, evacuation maps, accessible disaster plan, notice of relocation).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.15**: Admission and Resident Retention. *Verify:* paragraph (4) was truncated.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.16**: Admission Agreements (fees, 30-day and 60-day increase notices, complaint process, transportation, refund policy). *Verify:* later paragraphs were truncated.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.17**: Services in the Community (needs assessment, written care plan within 14 days of admission, activities, telephone access, restrictions on locking, proxy caregivers).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.19**: Additional Requirements for Certified Memory Care Centers. *Verify:* physical design paragraph (b) was not read.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.20**: Medications (certified medication aides, MAR, orders, storage, controlled substances, pharmacist and RN reviews).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.21**: Nutrition and Food Preparation. *Verify:* only some paragraphs were visible. A third-party source states that menus as served are kept 30 days. Confirm against the official text.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.24**: Residents' Files.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.25**: Supporting Residents Rights and Obtaining Feedback. *Verify:* the feedback paragraphs were not retrieved.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.26**: Procedures for Change in Resident's Condition (emergency response, DNR and advance directives, investigation of accidents, injuries and deaths).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.29**: Discharge or Transfer of Residents (30 days' written notice unless immediate transfer is required). *Verify:* later paragraphs were not retrieved.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.30**: Reports to the Department (Mattie's Call within 30 minutes; serious incident reports to DCH within 24 hours).

**Personal Care Homes (2–24 beds)**

- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62**: Personal Care Homes. Only rules .01–.09 were retrieved, and only .01–.06 were read in full.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.03**: Definitions (PCH). Includes the legal surrogate rule: no member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family members, may serve as a resident's legal surrogate.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.05**: Application for Permit (PCH).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.06**: Permits (PCH). *Verify:* the retrieved text was truncated.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.07**: Governing Body (PCH). *Verify:* the list of required policies was truncated.
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.08**: PCH Administrator Qualifications (summarized from fact-checked research, not full rule text; confirm against the official rule).
- **Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-62-.09**: PCH Workforce Qualifications and Training (summarized from fact-checked research; confirm against the official rule).
- **Rule 111-8-62 (staffing and change of ownership provisions)**: at least 30 days' written notice to DCH and residents of a change of ownership (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction). **The PCH staff ratio (1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and per 25 in non-waking hours) comes from third-party-hosted text and is NOT confirmed against current official text. Verify it before using it in any policy.**

**Other authorities and program requirements**

- **O.C.G.A. § 31-7-12.4**: Operation of memory care center; certificate required; staffing and training requirements (4-hour dementia orientation for all staff within 30 days; 16 hours of dementia training for direct care staff within 30 days, then 8 hours annually; documentation of course content, instructors, agendas and rosters).
- **DCH Schedule of Licensure Activity Fees**: application, license, memory care, late and replacement fees. Fee amounts are from fact-checked research; confirm the current schedule with DCH.
- **DCH ALC Application Checklist**: application documents, inspections, GCHEXS checks, GAHLES portal (updated 07/13/26): includes the Office of Health Planning Letter of Determination, State Fire Marshal report, electrician compliance form, water test where applicable, fingerprint checks, Affidavit of Compliance, and unannounced inspections.
- **Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators - Application for Initial Licensure as ALC or PCH Administrator (form dated 11.2022)**: administrator licensure requirements. Confirm the current fee and requirements with the Board.
- **CMS waiver 0112.R08.00**: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (expires 11/08/2027), the authority for CCSP and SOURCE, including Alternative Living Services in licensed personal care homes. Waivers do not pay room and board.
- **21st Century Cures Act (EVV)**: electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services, implemented by DCH. Applicable claims with dates of service on or after Sept 14, 2026 must go through EVV. **Whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself is unverified. Confirm with DCH.**

**Incorporated rules.** The ALC rules refer to other DCH chapters that should be on hand: Ch. 111-8-25 (permit fees and related requirements), Ch. 111-8-100 (governing body compliance oversight), Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans) and Ch. 111-8-12 (criminal background checks). These chapters were not retrieved in full for this manual, so obtain and review their current text.

### Regulators and contacts

Contact details are listed only where supplied. Where no phone or email is listed, use the website shown and confirm current contact information before publishing the manual.

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD)** | Permits and licenses PCHs and ALCs; conducts unannounced periodic inspections; issues memory care certificates | Email: pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov. Web: https://dch.georgia.gov/divisionsoffices/hfrd/facilities-provider-information/personal-care-homes |
| **DCH Office of Health Planning (OHP)** | Issues the Letter of Determination required with the initial ALC application | Web: https://dch.georgia.gov/con-applications-and-forms |
| **Georgia State Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators (Secretary of State)** | Licenses ALC administrators and administrators of 25+ bed PCHs | Phone: 404-424-9966. Web: https://sos.ga.gov/sites/default/files/forms/18%20Application%20-%20ALCA%20and%20PCHA%20Initial%20Licensure.pdf |
| **DCH Division of Medicaid (Medical Assistance Plans)** | Administers the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP and SOURCE); contracts with the 12 Area Agencies on Aging | Web: https://medicaid.georgia.gov/programs/all-programs/waiver-programs |
| **Area Agencies on Aging (statewide toll-free line)** | First point of contact for waiver assessment and screening; screening determines eligibility, urgency and waitlist placement | Phone: 866-552-4464 (866-55-AGING). Web: https://georgia.gov/apply-elderly-and-disabled-waiver-program |
| **Georgia DHS Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS)** | Determines Medicaid financial eligibility for the Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program; keeps the EDWP waiting list | Web: https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/medicaid/2131/ |
| **Georgia DHS Division of Aging Services** | Sets the monthly PCH room-and-board rate for SOURCE residents ($768 effective 1/1/2026, per secondary sources; confirm) | Web: https://www.georgiahealth.us/medicaid-waivers/ |
| **State Fire Marshal** | Fire safety inspection report (no violations, capacity load) dated within 12 months of application submission | Details in the DCH ALC Application Checklist: https://dch.georgia.gov/document/document/assisted-living-community-application-packet-0/download |
| **Georgia Medicaid GAMMIS provider enrollment** | Medicaid provider enrollment and revalidation; retroactive enrollment is not permitted | Web: https://www.mmis.georgia.gov/portal/ |
| **Georgia Department of Labor** | State unemployment insurance registration and tax rates | Web: https://dol.georgia.gov/faqs-employers/employers-faqs-unemployment-insurance |
| **Local zoning and planning officials** | Applicant must address local zoning and location requirements with the responsible local officials | Contact your local government; see https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/111-8-63 |

**Ombudsman.** Residents have a right of access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.). The assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone number must be posted in a common area (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-63-.25). Enter yours here: **[OMBUDSMAN NAME / ADDRESS / PHONE]**.

### Items to resolve before adoption

1. Read in full every rule flagged "verify" above, especially 111-8-63-.07 and 111-8-62-.07 (required policy lists), 111-8-63-.15, .16, .29 (admission, agreements, discharge), 111-8-63-.13 (safety and fire drills) and 111-8-63-.19 (memory care design).
2. Confirm the PCH staffing ratio and the PCH-specific text of ch. 111-8-62 rules beyond .06.
3. Confirm current fees, administrator licensure requirements and EVV applicability with DCH and the Board.
4. Fill in all [AGENCY NAME] and other bracketed placeholders, then have the governing body adopt the manual and train all staff.

This manual does not create any rule. If it conflicts with the current official text of a rule, the rule controls.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Assisted Living Communities (rule index .01-.34)
citations.requirement: Minimum standards for personal care homes licensed as assisted living communities (ALC, 25+ residents). The Secretary of State page and Cornell index list rules .01-.34, including .08 Community Leadership, .09 Workforce, .14 Emergency Preparedness, .19 Memory Care, .20 Medications, .26 Change in Condition, .29 Discharge and .30 Reports.

citations.title: Personal Care Homes (rules .01-.09 text retrieved)
citations.requirement: Governs personal care homes (2+ unrelated adults). Legal authority is O.C.G.A. Title 31, Chapters 2 and 7. A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license. The rules are mirrored for PCHs in the Secretary of State text; only .01-.06 were read in full here.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the policies must use. Examples: abuse; injury (includes pressure ulcers not properly cared for); assistive device (needs a physician/NP/PA order, a written care plan and resident consent); assisted self-preservation; chemical and physical restraints (bedrails, wheelchair safety bars, tight tucking and mitts count; alarm wristbands do not); limited nursing services (care completed within 7 days or intermittently); memory care center; medical alert system (DCH-approved); proxy caregiver; Mattie's-call-related elopement; owner (10% or more interest).

citations.title: Application for Permit
citations.requirement: The governing body applies on DCH forms. DCH will not act on an incomplete application or one without fees (per Ch. 111-8-25). Required: floor plan with window, door, common-area and room measurements plus .jpg photos; administrator or on-site manager name; full ownership disclosure (10%+ owners and registered agent); ownership or lease documentation; local zoning addressed with local officials; initial application must include a CPA financial stability affidavit (going concern for 2 years).

citations.title: Permits
citations.requirement: Valid permit required before admitting residents. Permit displayed conspicuously where residents and visitors see it. Not transferable. Must be returned and is no longer valid if the community moves to an unlicensed location, ownership changes, or the permit is suspended or revoked. Separate permit for each premises. May not exceed licensed capacity on the permit face. Must disclose ALC licensure classification in marketing. No other business may operate on the premises in a way that intrudes on residents' quiet enjoyment.

citations.title: Owner Governance
citations.requirement: The community must have a functioning governing body that oversees compliance with Ch. 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100. The governing body implements policies supporting dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy. Policies must at minimum direct staff and residents on: (a) services available, including memory care and proxy caregivers; (b) a staffing plan under which ratios rise as assisted-self-preservation residents increase; (c) admissions, discharges and immediate transfers that avoid admitting or retaining residents needing more care than the community is authorized or able to provide; (d) refunds on transfer or discharge; (e) staff training and evaluation; (f) house rules and enforcement; plus further items through investigation and reporting (list truncated in retrieved text; read the full paragraph before finalizing).

citations.title: Workforce Qualifications, Training and Staffing (amended eff. May 21, 2025)
citations.requirement: Full text read. (1) On-site manager and responsible staff 21+; no staff under 18 without line-of-sight supervision (17-year-old exception for a GA high-school nursing-assistant track). (2) All-staff training within 60 days. (3) Hands-on staff training within 60 days, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration. (4) At least 2 trained staff present at all times, one per occupied floor. (5) 24 CE hours in year one; (6) 16 hours annually after. (7) Training records. (10) TB screening and physical within 12 months before providing care. (11)-(13) Criminal background checks under Ch. 111-8-12. (14)-(15) Employment history; personnel files kept 3 years after departure. (17) No impairment on duty. (18) Average monthly ratio 1:15 awake waking hours and 1:20 non-waking for minimal-need residents; at least 2 direct care staff 24/7, one per occupied floor; RN or LPN on site 8 h/wk (1-30 residents), 16 (31-60), 24 (61-90), 40 (90+). (19) Sufficient staff time. (21) Staffing plans and schedules kept 1 year. (22) ID badges. (23) Medical alert system requirements.

citations.title: Community Accountability
citations.requirement: Records available to DCH inspectors. Inspection report disputes due within 10 days of receipt. Written plan of correction due within 10 days, with date-certain actions. Most recent inspection report and plan of correction displayed where residents and visitors see them. Website link to the previous 18 months of reports and plans if the community has a website. Keep an accurate licensed residential care profile. Services and marketing must match the license, profile and rules. Only a licensed ALC may hold itself out as offering assisted living care. No memory care center without a current certificate.

citations.title: Community Furnishings
citations.requirement: Furnishings maintained intact and functional. Name plate outside each resident's room unless declined. Closet or wardrobe and reading-adequate lighting in each room. Individual bed at least 36 x 72 inches with mattress at least 5 inches thick (4 if synthetic). No cots, roll-aways, double-decks, stacked bunks, hide-a-beds or studio couches in lieu of beds. Linens for residents needing linen service: at minimum 2 sheets, pillow, pillowcase, blanket, bedspread, towels and washcloth. Help hanging pictures. (Only some paragraphs were visible in the retrieved text.)

citations.title: Community Safety Precautions
citations.requirement: Interior and exterior kept clean, in good repair and free of unsafe conditions. Entrances, exits, sidewalks and escape routes kept free of hazards. Name and house number visible from the street. (Only (1), (11) and (12) were visible; fire drill and other paragraphs were not retrieved.)

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: Comply with Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans). Post evacuation maps with marked escape routes on each floor. Keep a clear accessible emergency route through common areas. The disaster plan is readily accessible to staff, residents and families and names the staff positions responsible for implementing it and obtaining emergency medical attention. Give timely notice of the relocation address to residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH if an emergency forces relocation.

citations.title: Admission and Resident Retention
citations.requirement: (1) Admission profile: age 18+; no active TB; no need for continuous medical or nursing care; no need for physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control; able to actively participate in transfers; able to participate in social and leisure activities. (2) The administrator or on-site manager must document the evaluation of applicants, including a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and documented added safety measures for registered sex offenders or violent offenders. A physician examination on DCH forms is referenced. (4) Community admission decisions (text truncated in retrieved copy).

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Plain-language agreement consistent with the licensed residential care profile. Must state all fees and what they cover. Written notice at least 30 days before any increase in personal-service charges and at least 60 days before any increase in room-and-board charges. Provisions for continuous assessment and referral or transfer on change of condition. A description of the complaint process. Transportation provisions, with emergency transport available at all times. A refund policy on death, transfer or discharge. Further items follow (truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: Services in the Community
citations.requirement: (1) Provide assisted living including protective care and watchful oversight. (2) Resident needs assessment covering family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and preferences. (3) Written care plan within 14 days of admission, updated at least annually and when needs change substantially or on assignment to a memory care center. (4) Daily social activities. (6) Operable non-pay telephone for staff emergency use and private resident access. (7) Do not restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident into or out of the bedroom. (8) Proxy caregiver options. (11) Periodic or short-term medical and nursing health services are not provided as community services; they are purchased by the resident (care planning, training, medication administration and competency checks excepted).

citations.title: Additional Requirements for Certified Memory Care Centers
citations.requirement: Applies if the community holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care or charges more for it. The licensed residential care profile must carry a written description with 12 elements (philosophy, how services differ, staffing and training, admission and screening criteria, assessment and reassessment triggers before the customary quarterly review, staffing patterns, physical environment and security, activities, fees, discharge criteria, emergency procedures, family involvement). Staffing: one dementia-trained direct care staff per 12 residents in waking hours and per 15 in non-waking hours (monthly average). RN or LPN hours in the center: 8 h/wk (1-12 residents), 16 (13-30), 24 (31-40), 40 (more than 40). Annual staff training. Physical design paragraph (b) not read.

citations.title: Medications
citations.requirement: Full text read. Residents capable of self-administration may keep and self-administer medications securely. Staff assistance is limited to listed tasks for unit or multi-dose packaged medications, including EpiPen use under a written protocol with a 911 call. Only certified medication aides (CMAs) may administer. The community must check the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry, run skills competency checks, use an RN or pharmacist for quarterly random observations, and have a pharmacist do quarterly drug regimen reviews. An RN, pharmacist or physician does annual competency reviews. Orders are required for all medications including OTC. New prescriptions within 48 hours and MAR updated within 48 hours. Daily MAR. Medications stored under lock and key; controlled substances in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction with a daily-updated log; duplicate keys on site; original containers; disposal per FDA/EPA guidance; liquid morphine limited to 50 ml per hospice patient.

citations.title: Nutrition and Food Preparation
citations.requirement: At least 3 regularly scheduled well-balanced meals per day, 7 days a week, plus therapeutic diets as ordered by the resident's healthcare provider. No more than 14 hours between the evening and morning meals. Nutrition per Recommended Daily Diet Allowances. At least one nutritious snack offered daily. Food must be clean, wholesome and safe. Menus dated and planned at least 1 week ahead for regular and therapeutic diets, posted or easily available, with resident input encouraged. Perishables held at or below 41 degrees F. A third-party reproduction states menus as served are kept 30 days. Only some paragraphs were visible.

citations.title: Residents' Files
citations.requirement: The administrator or on-site manager keeps an individual file for each resident. Confidential; disclosed only to the resident, representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents and those with written authorization. Available for inspection and copying by the resident or representative and by DCH. Contents include: identifying information; physician, hospital and pharmacy of choice; record of monetary transactions with itemized receipts; record and receipt of valuables held in safekeeping; health information (appraisals, diagnoses, diets, medications, orders); inventory of personal valuables; signed Resident's Rights form; signed admission agreement; powers of attorney; living will, DPOA-HC or Georgia advance directive (forms available at admission); signed end-of-life medical orders.

citations.title: Supporting Residents Rights and Obtaining Feedback
citations.requirement: Rights cannot be waived except by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow. Care must be adequate and appropriate. No punishment or harassment for enforcing rights. Rights to vote, choose activities and schedules, interact with the community, and privacy in the room (staff knock first). Free and private communication without staff censorship. Married residents may share a room, and no more than two residents may share a bedroom. Freedom from coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community. (u) A resident without a court commitment or authorized representative may self-discharge on 30 days written notice. (v) Access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.), with the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone posted in a common area. Paragraphs on feedback were not retrieved.

citations.title: Procedures for Change in Resident's Condition
citations.requirement: Full text read. On an accident or sudden adverse change the community acts immediately, notifies the representative or legal surrogate, and records the change and response in the resident file. For an unresponsive resident: hospice enrollee, call the hospice, then the health care agent, then EMS and CPR if no DNR. Valid DNR: honor it in good faith. Health care agent under O.C.G.A. 31-32-1 et seq.: call the agent, and if unavailable with no DNR call EMS and start CPR. No hospice, DNR or directive: call EMS and start CPR unless clearly futile and no physician, authorized RN or PA is on site. Staff need ready access to emergency numbers and resident information, including during transport. The administrator or on-site manager must start an immediate investigation of the cause of an accident, injury or death, report to the representative or legal surrogate, and keep copies in the resident file and a central quality-assurance file.

citations.title: Discharge or Transfer of Residents
citations.requirement: (1) Each admission agreement includes a written procedure for discharge and transfer. The administrator or on-site manager contacts the representative or legal surrogate when discharge or transfer is needed. The community gives 30 days written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required. Later paragraphs not retrieved.

citations.title: Reports to the Department
citations.requirement: Full text read. Call local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing (Mattie's Call Act). Report the start and end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement. Report serious incidents to DCH within 24 hours of the incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred: accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness; serious injury needing medical attention; rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation (Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act); external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation; an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record. Report contents: community and administrator names, incident date and discovery date, incident type and brief description, immediate corrective or preventive action. DCH may open a separate complaint investigation.

citations.title: Application for Permit (PCH)
citations.requirement: PCH application on DCH format with truthful disclosure. Sketch or drawing of the home and grounds showing windows, doors, room measurements and bed placement, plus ownership or lease documentation. Administrator or on-site manager name before the permit issues. Disclosure of owners with 10% or more and the registered agent. Local zoning addressed. A CPA financial stability affidavit is required for an initial application of 25 or more beds. No PCH may operate and no resident may be admitted without a current permit. No memory care center may operate without a current certificate.

citations.title: Permits (PCH)
citations.requirement: Valid permit before operating. Permit displayed conspicuously. May not exceed approved licensed capacity. Permit invalid and returned when the home ceases to operate, moves, or ownership changes (text truncated after this point in the retrieved copy).

citations.title: Governing Body (PCH)
citations.requirement: The governing body oversees compliance with Title 31 Ch. 7, and DCH Ch. 111-8-25, 111-8-62 and 111-8-100. It keeps DCH supplied with current contact information (name, email for notices, physical addresses, phones for the governing body and administrator or on-site manager) and makes staff accountable for delivering notices to it. Required policies cover services, admissions/discharges/immediate transfers, refunds, staff training and evaluation, house rules, rights, and medication management (list continues; truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: PCH Administrator Qualifications
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: for fewer than 25 beds, an associate's degree, or a GED/high school diploma plus 2 years' licensed PCH or healthcare experience, and age 21+. For 25+ beds, a valid Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license within 60 days of hire.

citations.title: PCH Workforce Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: on-site managers and responsible staff persons 21+; under-18 staff only under line-of-sight supervision; new staff work-related training including emergency first aid and CPR certification within 60 days.

citations.title: Definitions (PCH)
citations.requirement: Legal surrogate definition: no member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family members, may serve as a resident's legal surrogate. A copy of any power of attorney must be kept in the resident file. Also defines abuse, exploitation, physical and chemical restraint, memory care center, representative, and similar terms.

citations.title: Operation of memory care center; certificate required; staffing and training requirements
citations.requirement: Memory care centers: all staff get at least 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation within the first 30 days. Direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of dementia training within the first 30 days of working independently with dementia residents, then at least 8 hours annually. Keep documentation of course content, instructor qualifications, agendas and attendance rosters.

citations.cite: DCH Schedule of Licensure Activity Fees
citations.title: Application, license, memory care, late and replacement fees
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: $300 non-refundable application fee; annual license $350 (PCH 2-24 beds), $750 (ALC 25-50), $1,500 (ALC 51+); memory care certificate $200 per year; $150 late fee when 60 days past due; $50 permit replacement.

citations.title: ALC application documents, inspections, GCHEXS checks, GAHLES portal (updated 07/13/26)
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: DCH Office of Health Planning Letter of Determination; State Fire Marshal report with no violations and capacity load (within 12 months); electrician compliance form (within 6 months); private water test within 6 months if no city or county water; GCHEXS fingerprint checks for administrators and owners with 10%+ (letter within 12 months); communities are inspected without notice and policies must be available for review; Affidavit of Compliance.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services, implemented by DCH
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Georgia uses Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Personal support services under CCSP and SOURCE are listed under HCPCS T1019. Applicable claims with dates of service on or after Sept 14, 2026 must go through EVV. Whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself is unverified; confirm with DCH.

citations.title: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (expires 11/08/2027)
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: authority for CCSP and SOURCE, including Alternative Living Services in licensed personal care homes. Waivers do not pay room and board.

citations.cite: Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators - Application for Initial Licensure as ALC or PCH Administrator (form dated 11.2022)
citations.title: Administrator initial licensure application
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: $100 application fee plus $10 (paper) or $5 (online) processing fee. At least 1 year of full-time experience (1,560 hours in the preceding 12 months) plus a board-approved administration program. The license is biennial and expires Dec 31 of odd-numbered years. The Board's phone is 404-424-9966. Confirm the current fee.

citations.cite: Rule 111-8-62 (staffing and change of ownership provisions)
citations.title: PCH staffing ratios and 30-day change-of-ownership notice
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: at least 30 days written notice to DCH and residents of a change of ownership (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction). The PCH staff ratio of 1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and per 25 in non-waking hours comes from third-party-hosted text and is NOT confirmed against current official text; verify before use.

citations.title: Legal authority for Ch. 111-8-63 (Rule 111-8-63-.01)
citations.requirement: Statutory authority for the ALC rules; Rule .09 notes also cite O.C.G.A. 31-2-8, 31-2-9, 31-7-1 et seq. and 43-26-12.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing body, owners, administrator, on-site manager and responsible staff of [AGENCY NAME] (Personal Care Home under Ch. 111-8-62 and Assisted Living Community under Ch. 111-8-63)
policies.purpose: To establish who is legally responsible for [AGENCY NAME], how the governing body oversees compliance with Georgia licensure rules, and how duties are assigned to the administrator and staff so that residents receive safe, dignified care.
policies.policy: The governing body of [AGENCY NAME] is legally responsible for the operation of the community. It oversees compliance with the applicable Georgia rules: Ch. 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100 for an Assisted Living Community, and Title 31 Ch. 7 with Ch. 111-8-62, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100 for a Personal Care Home (C6, C35). Where the community is an LLC or corporation, the governing body authorizes the license application and signs the statement of responsibility, and the entity is the licensee (C3). The governing body designates an administrator. The administrator may also serve as on-site manager and responsible staff person except during the administrator's own absence, when another qualified person must be designated (C3). The on-site manager and every responsible staff person must be at least 21 years old (C8). The governing body adopts and enforces written policies that support the dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy of residents. At a minimum, these policies direct staff and residents on: services available (including memory care and proxy caregivers, if offered); a staffing plan under which staffing rises as the number of residents needing assisted self-preservation increases; admissions, discharges and immediate transfers that avoid admitting or keeping residents who need more care than the community is authorized or able to provide; refunds on transfer or discharge; staff training and evaluation; house rules and their enforcement; and investigation and reporting. A Personal Care Home policy set must also cover resident rights and medication management (C6, C35). The governing body keeps DCH supplied with current contact information and makes staff accountable for delivering DCH notices to it (C35). Each recurring compliance duty is assigned to one named person.

definitions.definition: The owner, board, partnership, or the governing body of the corporation or LLC that is legally responsible for the community's operation and holds the license.

The person designated by the governing body to manage day-to-day operations. For an Assisted Living Community, and for a Personal Care Home of 25 or more beds, the administrator must hold a license from the Georgia State Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators.
The person in charge of the community on site and the staff person designated to be in charge during the manager's absence. Each must be 21 or older (C8).
A resident's ability to evacuate with limited staff help in an emergency; the number of residents who need such help drives the staffing plan (C3, C6).
A person with a 10 percent or greater ownership interest in the community (C3).

procedures: The governing body meets at least annually and whenever a significant regulatory or operational issue arises. The secretary records minutes, which are kept at [ADDRESS].

The governing body designates the administrator in writing and records the name on the DCH application and any later update. The administrator's license from the Georgia State Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators is verified and a copy is placed in the administrator's file before the administrator starts.

The governing body designates in writing an on-site manager and responsible staff persons for every shift. Human Resources confirms each is 21 or older before designation and keeps the proof in the personnel file (C8).
The administrator posts or maintains a written coverage schedule so that a designated responsible staff person is always on site, including when the administrator or manager is absent.

The governing body reviews and approves the written policies on each topic required for the community type (services, staffing plan, admissions/discharges/immediate transfers, refunds, staff training and evaluation, house rules, investigation and reporting, and for a PCH rights and medication management). Approval is recorded in the minutes with the effective date.

The administrator prepares a written staffing plan that increases staffing as the number of residents needing assisted self-preservation rises. The governing body approves it and the administrator re-reviews it whenever the resident mix changes and at least quarterly (C6, C8).

The administrator may not accept admissions that exceed what the governing body has determined the community is authorized and able to serve. The governing body reviews admissions and discharge trends and any immediate transfers at each meeting (C6).

The governing body keeps DCH current on its name, email address for notices, physical addresses and phone numbers for both the governing body and the administrator or on-site manager. Changes are sent to DCH at pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov within [NUMBER] days after the change, and the change is logged (C35).

The administrator instructs all staff that any DCH notice, inspection report or correspondence received at the community must be given to the administrator the same day. The administrator forwards it to the governing body contact, [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT NAME], within one business day (C35).

The administrator maintains a Duty Assignment Matrix naming one responsible person for each recurring duty: permit renewal and fees, training calendar, TB screening and physical tracking, background checks, quarterly pharmacist drug regimen review, RN or LPN hours, staffing calculations, inspection response, and policy updates.

The governing body reviews a written report from the administrator at each meeting covering census, staffing against the plan, training status, incidents and DCH reports, grievances, inspection results and plan-of-correction progress.

The administrator confirms that required staff training occurs within 60 days of hire, that continuing education (24 hours in year one, 16 hours annually after) is scheduled, and that training records are kept. The governing body reviews completion rates at least quarterly (C8).
The administrator conducts a written evaluation of each employee at the end of the first 90 days and at least annually thereafter, and files it in the personnel file.
The governing body adopts written house rules and the administrator ensures they are given to residents and enforced consistently and without retaliation.
If the administrator's employment ends, the governing body names an interim administrator or on-site manager within [NUMBER] days and notifies DCH of the new name and contact details (C35).
The governing body reviews this policy at least annually and whenever the rules change.

responsibilities.duty: Holds legal responsibility; oversees compliance; adopts, reviews and approves policies and the staffing plan; designates the administrator; keeps DCH contact information current.
Manages daily operations; implements policies; maintains the Duty Assignment Matrix; ensures staffing, training and personnel requirements are met; reports to the governing body.
Is on site and in charge during assigned shifts; ensures DCH notices and incident information reach the administrator promptly.
Verifies age, licensure and personnel file contents; tracks training and evaluation dates.

documentation: Governing body minutes and written resolutions
Written designation of administrator, on-site manager and responsible staff persons
Administrator license verification
Approved policy set with effective dates
Written staffing plan and revisions
Log of contact-information updates sent to DCH
Duty Assignment Matrix
Administrator reports to governing body
Employee training records and evaluations

policies.title: Licensure, Permit Posting and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator and front-office staff of [AGENCY NAME] (PCH and ALC)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds a current DCH permit before admitting any resident, displays it, never exceeds licensed capacity, pays required fees on time and meets permit-change obligations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not admit or serve any resident until the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), Healthcare Facility Regulation Division, has issued a current permit. An Assisted Living Community permit is required for assisted living care (C5). A Personal Care Home may not operate or admit a resident without a current permit (C33). No memory care center is operated without a current DCH certificate. The permit is displayed conspicuously where residents and visitors can see it (C5, C34). The community never exceeds the licensed capacity on the face of the permit (C5, C34). A separate permit is held for each premises (C5). The permit is not transferable. It is invalid and must be returned to DCH if the community moves to an unlicensed location, ownership changes, or the permit is suspended or revoked (C5, C34). A Personal Care Home gives DCH and residents at least 30 days' written notice of a change of ownership (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction) (C53). The community pays all DCH fees on time and keeps the application documents current.

definitions.definition: The DCH-issued authorization to operate at a specific premises up to the licensed capacity printed on its face.
The maximum number of residents shown on the permit.
Any transfer of ownership of the licensee that invalidates the existing permit and requires notice to DCH and residents.
The DCH online system through which applications are filed, per DCH's ALC application checklist (C49).
The fingerprint-based background check required for administrators and owners with 10 percent or more interest (C49).

procedures: Before the first admission, the administrator verifies that the DCH permit is issued, reads the permit face for the licensed capacity, premises address and classification, and records the verification date in the Licensure Log.
The administrator posts the permit conspicuously in the main entrance or lobby where residents and visitors see it, and checks weekly that it is still displayed.

The admissions coordinator checks the census against licensed capacity before accepting any admission. Admissions that would exceed capacity are declined, and the check is initialed on the admission checklist.

For an initial ALC application, the governing body assembles and files through the GAHLES portal: the application on DCH forms; the DCH Office of Health Planning Letter of Determination; the State Fire Marshal report with no violations and capacity load (dated within 12 months); the electrician compliance form (within 6 months); a private water test (within 6 months) if there is no city or county water; GCHEXS fingerprint letters for the administrator and every 10 percent or more owner (within 12 months); the CPA financial stability affidavit (going concern for 2 years); floor plan with measurements and .jpg photos; ownership or lease documents; the Affidavit of Compliance; and the application fee (C4, C49).

For an initial PCH application, the governing body submits the DCH-format application with truthful disclosures; a sketch of the home and grounds showing windows, doors, room measurements and bed placement; ownership or lease documentation; the administrator or on-site manager's name; disclosure of 10 percent or more owners and the registered agent; and, for an initial application of 25 or more beds, the CPA financial stability affidavit (C33).
The governing body addresses local zoning with local officials before applying and keeps written confirmation in the licensure file (C4, C33).
The administrator does not submit an incomplete application or one without fees, because DCH will not act on it (C4).

The administrator pays DCH fees on the due dates shown on the schedule: $300 non-refundable application fee; annual license fee of $350 (PCH 2-24 beds), $750 (ALC 25-50 beds) or $1,500 (ALC 51 or more beds); $200 memory care certificate; and $50 permit replacement. A $150 late fee applies when payment is 60 days past due. Before each payment the administrator confirms the amount against the current DCH Schedule of Licensure Activity Fees, which was last reviewed in October 2024 (C48).
The administrator calendars the license renewal and fee due dates 90 days in advance and records them in the Licensure Log, with a back-up reminder to the governing body contact.
If the permit is lost or damaged, the administrator requests a replacement from DCH, pays the replacement fee, and posts a copy until it arrives.

At least 30 days before any planned change of ownership of a PCH (60 days when bankruptcy or eviction is impending), the governing body delivers written notice to DCH and to every resident or representative, and keeps proof of delivery (C53). The administrator confirms with DCH what new permit application is needed.
If the community is to move, close, or lose its permit, the administrator returns the permit to DCH, stops admissions immediately, and starts the relocation planning in ADM-05.

The administrator maintains a log of variances, waivers and deemed-status requests. Before relying on any of them, the administrator reads the full current rule text and keeps DCH's written approval on file.
The administrator keeps current policies, resident records, personnel files and other required records available to DCH inspectors at any time, because inspections are unannounced (C49).

The administrator keeps DCH contact details in the front-office binder: Personal Care Home Team, pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov; DCH telephone (404) 656-4507; 2 Martin Luther King Jr. Dr. SE, East Tower, Atlanta, GA 30334.
The administrator reviews this policy each quarter against the current DCH fee schedule and the Secretary of State rules site.

responsibilities.duty: Files applications, signs affidavits, pays fees, gives change-of-ownership notices and ensures permit validity.
Maintains the Licensure Log, posts the permit, enforces the capacity limit, calendars renewals and responds to DCH.
Checks census against licensed capacity before every admission.
Confirm the permit remains displayed and route any DCH correspondence to the administrator the same day.

documentation: Current permit and any memory care certificate
Licensure Log with verification and renewal dates
Application packet copies and portal confirmations
Fire Marshal, electrician, water test and GCHEXS documents with dates
Fee payment receipts
Change-of-ownership notices with proof of delivery
Variance, waiver and deemed-status log
Weekly permit-posting check record

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body and all staff who use or maintain [AGENCY NAME]'s Policy & Procedure Manual
policies.purpose: To keep the Policy & Procedure Manual current with Georgia rules, controlled, available to staff and ready for DCH review at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written Policy & Procedure Manual that covers every topic the governing body is required to address (C6). The manual is available for review at all times, because DCH inspects communities without notice and policies must be available during inspections (C49). Records are open to DCH inspectors (C9). Every policy carries a version number, effective date, approver and revision history. Each policy is reviewed at least annually, a facility standard that is not itself a rule requirement, and sooner when rules change. Rule 111-8-63-.09 was amended effective May 21, 2025 (including staffing ratios and medical alert systems) (C8). Further DCH amendments to the PCH rules were proposed in February 2025, and their final adoption has not been verified, so the administrator checks the Secretary of State rules site each quarter. The manual includes the policies the rules require by name: a medical alert system policy (C8), a medication policy, a refund policy, a discharge and transfer procedure included in the admission agreement, and a proxy caregiver policy if proxy caregivers are used.

definitions.definition: A policy with a version number, effective date, named approver and revision history, issued from a single master copy.
The one authoritative copy of the Policy & Procedure Manual kept by the administrator.
A DCH-approved system for resident emergency alerting, which must be supported by a written policy (C3, C8).

procedures: The administrator keeps the master manual, electronic and printed, at [ADDRESS] in a location known to all staff and immediately available to a DCH inspector.
The administrator assigns each policy a number, version, effective date, approver and revision history, and enters it in the Policy Index.

The administrator reviews the Secretary of State rules site for Ch. 111-8-62, 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100 each quarter, records the date and any changes found in the Regulatory Watch Log, and tracks pending DCH rulemaking.
When a rule changes, the administrator identifies affected policies within 10 business days, drafts revisions, and submits them to the governing body for approval.
The governing body approves revisions in writing. The approval date becomes the effective date.

The administrator replaces superseded copies at every location where the manual is kept, retains one archived copy of each superseded version for at least [NUMBER] years, and marks the old copy as superseded.
Within 7 days of any material change, the administrator trains affected staff and obtains signed acknowledgment, which is placed in the personnel file.
New employees read and sign acknowledgment of the policies relevant to their position during the 60-day training period (C8).

The administrator verifies that the manual contains the policies the rules name specifically: medical alert system, medication, refunds, discharge and transfer, and proxy caregiver if used. A gap list is kept and closed within 30 days (C6, C8).
If the community has a website, the administrator confirms that the policies posted there match the controlled version (C9).
At each annual review, the governing body reviews every policy for accuracy against current rules and actual practice, and signs the review page.
Before a DCH inspection or whenever DCH arrives, the administrator or on-site manager gives the inspector immediate access to the manual and records (C9, C49).

responsibilities.duty: Approves new and revised policies and signs the annual review.
Maintains the master manual, Policy Index and Regulatory Watch Log; conducts quarterly rule checks; trains staff on changes.
Read assigned policies, sign acknowledgments and follow current versions only.

documentation: Master Policy & Procedure Manual with version histories
Policy Index
Regulatory Watch Log with quarterly check dates
Governing body approval records and annual review signature page
Staff acknowledgment forms
Archive of superseded versions
Gap list for required-by-name policies

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, quality assurance designee, consultant pharmacist, RN or LPN, and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To use information from incidents, medication oversight, staffing records and reports to DCH to find problems early, protect residents and improve care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality assurance (QA) program built around the central QA file that Georgia requires for accident, injury and death investigations (C25). When an accident, injury or death occurs, the administrator or on-site manager starts an immediate investigation of the cause, reports the findings to the resident's representative or legal surrogate, and keeps copies in the resident's file and in the central QA file (C25). The QA program also reviews quarterly random medication-administration observations by an RN or pharmacist and quarterly pharmacist drug regimen reviews (C19), the monthly average staffing calculations documented on DCH forms (C8), medical alert system documentation (C8), serious incidents reported to DCH within 24 hours (C29), and inspection findings and plans of correction. No separate QAPI committee is required by the rule text reviewed. The committee structure and meeting schedule described below are the facility's own standards.

definitions.definition: A single file holding all accident, injury and death investigation reports for review.

An event reportable to DCH within 24 hours, such as an unanticipated death, a serious injury needing medical attention, abuse, neglect or exploitation, a disaster affecting safe operation, or a criminal record acquired by an owner, director or employee (C29).
Includes a pressure ulcer that is not properly cared for (C3).

procedures: The administrator designates a QA lead, [QA LEAD NAME], and forms a QA committee of the administrator, QA lead, RN or LPN, consultant pharmacist (as available) and a direct-care representative. The committee meets at least quarterly.

Immediately after any accident, injury or death, the on-site manager secures the scene, ensures the resident receives care, and notifies the administrator. The administrator or on-site manager starts the investigation immediately (C25).

Within 24 hours the investigator completes the incident report with the resident's name, date, time, witnesses, cause, response and corrective action, and gives a copy to the resident's representative or legal surrogate. Copies go in the resident's file and in the central QA file (C25).

The administrator decides within 24 hours whether the event meets a DCH 24-hour reporting category and makes the report under the Reports to DCH policy (C29). The QA lead logs each report date and time.

Each quarter the RN or pharmacist performs random observations of medication administration, and the pharmacist performs a drug regimen review of the resident records. The QA lead files both reports and tracks every finding to closure (C19).

Each month the administrator completes the monthly average staffing calculation on the DCH form and compares it with the staffing plan. Any shortfall is entered in the QA log with a corrective action (C8).
Each quarter the QA lead reviews medical alert system documentation, including tests, response times and failures (C8).

The QA lead compiles a quarterly dashboard: falls and injuries by type, medication errors, pressure injuries, elopements and missing-resident events, hospital transfers, grievances, serious incidents reported, staffing variances and training completion.
The committee reviews the central QA file and dashboard for trends by resident, location, shift and cause, and agrees on corrective actions with an owner and a due date.
The committee reviews DCH inspection findings and plan-of-correction progress at each meeting.
The administrator verifies that each corrective action was completed, and reviews results at the next meeting. Actions that did not work are revised.
The QA lead writes a summary for the governing body after each committee meeting. The governing body signs to show review.
QA records are retained at least [NUMBER] years and are available to DCH inspectors.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews QA summaries and supports corrective actions with resources.
Starts investigations, decides on DCH reportability, chairs the QA committee and verifies corrective actions.
Maintains the central QA file, logs and dashboard; tracks findings to closure.
Perform quarterly observations and drug regimen reviews and report findings.
Report incidents and concerns immediately.

documentation: Central QA file of accident, injury and death investigations
Incident reports with representative notification
Quarterly medication observation and pharmacist drug regimen review reports
Monthly staffing calculation forms
Medical alert system review records
Log of DCH reports made, with dates and times
Quarterly QA dashboard and committee minutes
Corrective action tracking log

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, billing and admissions staff, and all employees and contractors of [AGENCY NAME] participating in Medicaid (Alternative Living Services)
policies.purpose: To prevent fraud, waste and abuse, ensure accurate billing, and keep [AGENCY NAME] in good standing as a Medicaid waiver provider.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered and documented, and follows federal and state rules for the Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver Program (CCSP and SOURCE), which includes Alternative Living Services (ALS) in licensed personal care homes (C51). This policy applies if the community enrolls as a Medicaid ALS provider. The community is enrolled in Georgia Medicaid (GAMMIS) before it bills; retroactive enrollment is not permitted, and providers who did not revalidate by July 1, 2026 were suspended. If personal support services (HCPCS T1019) are billed under CCSP or SOURCE, they are recorded through the state's electronic visit verification (EVV) system, Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Claims with dates of service on or after September 14, 2026 must go through EVV (C50). The administrator confirms with DCH whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself, because that point is unverified. The waiver does not pay room and board, which the resident pays (C51). The community will not offer, pay, solicit or accept anything of value to induce referrals. It does not employ or contract with excluded persons. It discloses ownership information, and reports any criminal record acquired by an owner, director or employee to DCH within 24 hours of reasonable cause to believe it occurred, as required by DCH's reporting rules. Anyone may report a compliance concern without fear of retaliation.

definitions.definition: A claim for payment that the provider knows is false, including billing for services not delivered or not documented.
Electronic visit verification: electronic capture of the service type, individual served, date, location, provider and times of Medicaid personal care visits.
A person or entity barred from participating in federal health care programs, listed by the HHS Office of Inspector General or on Georgia Medicaid sanction lists.
The waiver service under which eligible residents receive services in a licensed personal care home (C51).
The resident-paid housing and meal charge, not paid by the waiver.

procedures: The governing body designates a Compliance Officer, [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME], who reports directly to the governing body and has authority to review billing and records.

Before billing, the administrator completes GAMMIS Medicaid provider enrollment and keeps the approval letter and provider number on file. Revalidation due dates are placed on the compliance calendar 120 days ahead.

The administrator confirms current ALS rates, billing rules and any EVV requirement against the DCH Medicaid provider manual and by direct inquiry to DCH before the first claim, and files the written response.

If T1019 personal support services are billed, the administrator arranges access to Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+, trains staff to log each visit in real time, and confirms the data matches the service plan before any claim dated on or after September 14, 2026 is submitted (C50).

Before each claim, the billing staff member checks that the service was authorized by the case manager or assessing agency, delivered, documented, and within dates and units authorized. Discrepancies are held and reported to the Compliance Officer.

The community collects room and board only in the amount permitted for waiver residents, which the resident pays directly. The community does not bill Medicaid for room and board and does not charge residents for services the waiver covers (C51). The current monthly room-and-board amount ($768 effective January 1, 2026, per secondary sources) is verified with the DHS Division of Aging Services before it is put in any agreement.

Before hire or contract, and at least monthly afterward, HR screens every owner, administrator, employee and contractor against the OIG exclusion list and Georgia Medicaid sanction lists, and keeps dated screening records. Anyone found excluded is removed from all duties immediately and the matter is reported to the Compliance Officer.
Owners with 10 percent or more interest, and administrators, are disclosed to DCH and Medicaid as required, and the administrator keeps the ownership disclosure current (C49).

The administrator reports any criminal record acquired by an owner, director or employee to DCH within 24 hours of reasonable cause to believe it occurred, as required by DCH's reporting rules, and logs the report.
No staff member may give or accept money, gifts or other value in exchange for referring residents. Marketing and referral relationships are reviewed by the Compliance Officer before they begin.
All employees receive compliance training on hire and annually, covering false claims, anti-kickback rules, EVV, documentation, and how to report concerns. Attendance is recorded.
Staff may report concerns to the Compliance Officer, the administrator or the governing body, anonymously if they wish, at [PHONE]. Retaliation is prohibited and is grounds for discipline.
The Compliance Officer investigates each report promptly, documents findings, corrects billing errors, repays any overpayment within 60 days of identifying it, and informs the governing body.
The Compliance Officer conducts a quarterly audit of a sample of claims against service documentation and reports results to the governing body.
All billing and compliance records are retained at least [NUMBER] years and are available to DCH and Medicaid reviewers.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the Compliance Officer, receives quarterly reports and ensures corrective action.
Runs the program, training, audits and investigations.
Maintains enrollment and revalidation, confirms rates and EVV rules with DCH, and ensures accurate documentation.
Verify authorization and documentation before billing.
Record services truthfully and report concerns.

documentation: GAMMIS enrollment and revalidation records
Written DCH confirmation on ALS rates and EVV applicability
EVV visit data and reconciliation records
Monthly OIG and Georgia sanction list screening records
Compliance training attendance
Compliance reports and investigation files
Quarterly claim audit reports
Ownership disclosure records
DCH reports of criminal records

policies.title: Licensed Residential Care Profile, Marketing and Licensure-Classification Accuracy
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, marketing and admissions staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure everything [AGENCY NAME] tells the public matches its license, its DCH licensed residential care profile and the Georgia rules, so no one is misled about the services offered.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps an accurate, current licensed residential care profile on file with DCH once the electronic system is available (C9). The services it provides match the profile, the license and the rules. All marketing, including the website, brochures, tours, signs, online listings and referral materials, matches the community's licensure classification, the profile and the rules (C9). Marketing for an Assisted Living Community discloses the ALC licensure classification (C5). Only a licensed Assisted Living Community may hold itself out as offering assisted living care. A community holding only a Personal Care Home permit does not do so (C9). The community does not advertise or operate a memory care center until DCH issues the memory care certificate (C9). If the community holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care, or charges more for it, it is a memory care center, and the licensed residential care profile must contain the written description with the 12 required elements (C18). No other business may operate on the premises in a way that intrudes on residents' quiet enjoyment (C5).

definitions.definition: The DCH-required description of the community's services, staffing, and other features that must be kept accurate and current.
The category under which DCH has permitted the community: Personal Care Home (2 to 24 beds) or Assisted Living Community (25 or more beds licensed for assisted living care).
A community or unit that holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care or charges more for it, and which must hold a DCH certificate.
Any public statement, advertisement or representation suggesting the community offers a type of care.

procedures: The administrator holds the licensed residential care profile and updates it within [NUMBER] days of any change to services, staffing, fees, or physical environment. Each submission to DCH is dated and filed.

The administrator compares the profile against actual services each quarter, using a checklist covering services offered, staffing, admission and retention criteria, fees and any memory care information, and records the result.
Before any marketing item is released, the administrator reviews it against the permit, classification, profile and rules and signs the approval on the marketing review form.
ALC marketing states the ALC licensure classification. Marketing for a PCH does not use the term 'assisted living' as a service description unless the community holds an ALC license (C5, C9).

Marketing and admissions staff are trained to describe only the services the community is licensed and able to provide. They are told not to promise services the community cannot provide or services outside its retention limits (see ADM-04).
The community does not use the words 'memory care', 'dementia care' or equivalent terms in any advertising, signage, tour script or fee schedule until DCH issues the memory care certificate (C9).

If the community plans memory care, the governing body applies to DCH first and, before the profile is changed, prepares the written description with the 12 elements: philosophy; how services differ; staffing and training; admission and screening criteria; assessment and reassessment triggers before the customary quarterly review; staffing patterns; physical environment and security; activities; fees; discharge criteria; emergency procedures; and family involvement (C18).

If memory care is approved, the community staffs to the memory care ratios and RN or LPN hours required by the rule, schedules annual dementia training, and keeps those records (C18). Staffing details are in the Workforce policies.
The community maintains a current copy of the profile in the front office and gives a copy to any prospective resident who asks, so that the written description matches what was said in the tour.
The administrator reviews the community's website, online directory listings and social media at least quarterly and corrects or removes inaccurate statements within 5 business days.

The administrator does not permit another business operating on the premises in a way that intrudes on residents' quiet enjoyment (C5). Any proposed outside business, vendor service or event space use is reviewed by the administrator and governing body before it begins.
Complaints about inaccurate marketing are handled under the Grievances policy and corrected promptly.
The administrator retains copies of all marketing materials, with dates used, for at least [NUMBER] years.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the classification and certificates match services; approves memory care plans.
Maintains the profile, approves all marketing, performs quarterly accuracy reviews.
Use only approved materials and describe services accurately.

documentation: Current licensed residential care profile and submission history
Quarterly profile-to-practice accuracy checklists
Marketing review and approval forms
Copies of marketing materials with use dates
Website and online listing review records
Memory care written description (if applicable)
Memory care certificate (if applicable)

policies.title: DCH Inspections, Inspection Reports and Plans of Correction
policies.applies_to: Personal Care Homes (Ch. 111-8-62) and Assisted Living Communities (Ch. 111-8-63): Administrator, on-site managers, governing body, all staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully with Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH) Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD) inspections, answers inspection reports on time, and gives residents and visitors access to the community's inspection results.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] expects DCH to inspect without notice and keeps itself ready for inspection at all times. Resident, personnel, financial and other required records are available to properly identified DCH representatives at any time (Rule 111-8-63-.10). The Administrator makes sure this Policy and Procedure Manual is available for review on site. Any written disagreement with an inspection report, and any written plan of correction, is filed with DCH within 10 days of receipt of the report. Each plan of correction lists specific actions with date-certain completion dates. The most recent inspection report and plan of correction are displayed where residents and visitors normally find information. If [AGENCY NAME] has a website, it carries a prominent link to every inspection report and plan of correction from the previous 18 months. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against any resident, family member or staff member who speaks with surveyors.

definitions.definition: The written findings DCH issues after an inspection, survey or complaint investigation.
A written response to cited deficiencies stating the corrective actions, who is responsible, and the date each action will be complete.
A specific calendar date by which a corrective action will be finished, not a general statement such as "ongoing" or "soon."
The date [AGENCY NAME] receives the report by hand delivery, mail, fax or electronic delivery. This is the date the 10-day clock starts.

procedures: Keep a current inspection-readiness binder or electronic folder, and make this Manual available on site for surveyors on request.

When surveyors arrive, the first staff member on duty greets them, asks for identification, and calls the Administrator or on-site manager immediately. If neither is on site, the senior staff member on duty follows the call list posted at the front desk.
Verify the identification of every person claiming to represent DCH. Record names, titles and arrival and departure times in the Inspection Log.

Give surveyors the records they request, including resident files, personnel files, training records, staffing plans and schedules, medication records, and the licensed residential care profile. The Administrator or designee keeps a list of everything copied or removed and does not refuse access to records.
Direct staff to answer surveyor questions truthfully and to ask for the Administrator if they are unsure. Residents are free to speak privately with surveyors.
The Administrator or designee attends the exit conference, takes notes, asks for clarification of each finding, and records the date and time.
